record.paper_title: Exact results and open questions in first principle functional RG
record.original_question: Starting from a nonzero bare temperature for a pinned elastic manifold, how does the flow toward T_L = T L^{-θ} → 0 produce a well-defined zero-temperature critical theory with all ambiguities resolved, and how can information about the outer region R(u) for u = O(1) be matched to the derivatives of R(u) at u = 0 that require the thermal boundary layer u ∼ T_L?

evidence.quote: An outstanding question in FRG, i.e. how temperature regularizes the otherwise singular flow of T = 0 FRG, maps to the viscous layer regularization of inertial range Burgers turbulence (i.e. to the construction of the inviscid limit).

The ultimate goal is to understand how a critical theory emerges in the large system size limit L → ∞, i.e. how, starting from a non zero bare temperature, the limit TL = T L−θ → 0 can produce an asymptotic "zero temperature theory" with all ambiguities resolved. It requires solving the so-called matching problem: one wants to connect information about e.g. R(u) for u ∼ O(1) (which is what the ǫ expansion a priori computes), to derivatives of R(u) at u = 0, needed to compute correlations, which a priori requires knowledge of the function within the TBL u ∼ TL.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the functional renormalization group (FRG) flow for a d-dimensional elastic manifold of linear size L pinned by quenched disorder, parameterized by the running second cumulant R_l(u) of the disorder (a function of the relative displacement field u ∈ R^N) and the rescaled temperature T_l = T e^{-θ l} along the RG scale l = log(L/a). At zero temperature the FRG flow is known to drive R(u) toward a non-analytic fixed-point function exhibiting a cusp at u = 0, while at any positive temperature the flow rounds the cusp inside a thermal boundary layer (TBL) of width u ∼ T_L = T L^{-θ}.

Develop a controlled construction of the inviscid (zero-temperature) limit of this FRG flow with the following properties:

1. Starting from a strictly positive bare temperature, show that as L → ∞ (so that T_L = T L^{-θ} → 0) the running effective action converges to a well-defined critical theory in which all ambiguities arising from the cusp non-analyticity (sign choices, values of derivatives at u = 0, products of distributions) are uniquely fixed by the T > 0 regularization.

2. Solve the associated matching problem: given the analytic "outer" function R(u) on the scale u = O(1) (as computed, e.g., by an ε-expansion around the upper critical dimension), determine the left/right derivatives R^{(k)}(0^+) and the higher-order moments of R(u) inside the boundary layer u ∼ T_L that are required to compute physical correlation functions, by means of explicit matching relations between the outer expansion and the inner TBL expansion.

Provide both an existence-and-uniqueness statement for the inviscid limit and explicit matching formulas (analogous to those known in inviscid-limit constructions for the Burgers equation) valid in arbitrary dimension d and for arbitrary number of components N.
artifact.status_search_result: The matching problem between the thermal boundary layer and the zero-temperature non-analytic FRG fixed point has been solved in detail only for d = 0 (the toy/single-particle limit), where it yields the T = 0 beta function with ambiguities removed up to four loops. For general d (and the analogy with the inviscid limit of Burgers turbulence), the construction of a unique zero-temperature critical theory and the full matching of the outer R(u) to TBL derivatives remain open or only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: Chaos in the thermal regime for pinned manifolds via functional RG
status_evidence.snippet: essentially non-perturbative thermal boundary layer (TBL) exists in the running effective action at T>0 ... how thermal correlations determined deep in the TBL can be retrieved as u=0+ limits in the non-analytic T=0 effective action, a formidable matching problem solved in detail for d=0
status_evidence.claim: The TBL matching problem is solved in d=0 but remains a 'formidable' open problem in higher d.

status_evidence.title: Thermal fluctuations in pinned elastic systems: field theory of rare events and droplets
status_evidence.snippet: thermal boundary layer extends to all cumulants of the disorder ... truncation to the second cumulant ... is not strictly consistent at T>0
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the matching/inviscid-limit construction is incomplete beyond d=0.
